channel.title: Keylink Transport Blog
channel.description: Freight industry analysis, cross-border trucking, and logistics strategy from Keylink Transport, a BC-based full truckload carrier.

item.title: The Cheap Freight Is Gone: Diesel Spikes, Capacity Tightens, and the Rate Reset Is Already Here
item.description: Canadian truck-to-load ratios hit 2.71 in July, the tightest in a year, diesel jumped 39.5 cents in two weeks, and truckload spot rates are running 43% above last year. What the 2026 cost reset means for 2027 contracts, and what shippers should do before renewal season.

item.title: Two Bills, One Morning: What the Carney-Trump Tariff War Does to Goods and Fuel Prices
item.description: US 50% tariffs on about US$20 billion of Canadian goods took effect August 22, and Canada retaliates September 8, the same day the federal fuel tax holiday ends. What the stacking does to goods prices, diesel, and cross-border freight, plus what shippers should do before the deadline.

item.title: One Highway Left: How BC's August Wildfires Are Rerouting Freight, and What the Detours Cost
item.description: BC has been under a provincial state of emergency since August 8 with more than 100 fires burning and 20,000 people evacuated. Highway 1, Highway 3, and Highway 97 all closed this summer, leaving the Coquihalla carrying the load. What the closures cost industry, and how carriers reroute around them.

item.title: The Heist Is Now an Email: How Freight Fraud Replaced the Cargo Heist in Canada
item.description: Cargo thefts across the US and Canada fell 26% in Q2 2026 while losses more than doubled to $304.6 million. Organized crime traded the crowbar for carrier impersonation, double brokering, and fictitious pickups. What the data shows, and how shippers verify who is actually holding their freight.

item.title: The Trailer Is Not a Warehouse: Canada's 2026 Industrial Space Squeeze and the Freight Bill Nobody Quotes
item.description: Canada's industrial availability rate sat at 6.2% in Q2 2026, and Toronto, Calgary, and Vancouver are tighter still. When warehouse space runs short, trailers become storage and shippers pay for it in detention, dwell, and lost capacity. The numbers, and what to do about them.

item.title: The Long Weekend Squeeze: How BC Day Bottlenecks Canadian Freight, and How Keylink Plans Around It
item.description: BC Day on Monday, August 3, 2026 closes docks, thins the border, and lands on the deadliest driving stretch of summer. Here is how Canada's August long weekend compresses the freight week and how Keylink mitigates the risk.

item.title: Speak English, or Park It: What the US Roadside Language Crackdown Means for Canadian Cross-Border Truckers
item.description: Since June 2025 the US puts commercial drivers out of service for failing a roadside English check, and Canadian cross-border drivers get no border-zone exemption like the US-Mexico line has. What the FMCSA ELP rule means, what it costs, and whether Canada should follow.

item.title: One Country, Two Licences: Quebec Stops Trusting Ontario's New Truck Drivers, and the Crackdown Is Just Starting
item.description: As of July 9, 2026, Quebec road-tests new Ontario truck drivers before recognizing their licence. The scathing Ontario training audit behind it, the CRA's Driver Inc crackdown, and what Canada's trucking compliance summer means for shippers.

item.title: The Half-Load Paradox: Why Partial and LTL Freight Is Out-Earning Full Truckloads in 2026
item.description: Partial and LTL half loads are out-earning full truckloads in 2026. Here is the data behind the inversion, why it is a market distortion rather than real efficiency, and what it means for Canadian shippers.

item.title: The CUSMA Clock Hits Zero: What the July 1 USMCA Review Means for Canadian Cross-Border Trucking
item.description: On July 1, 2026 the mandatory six-year review of CUSMA (USMCA) begins. Here is what the joint review actually decides, why it lands hardest on cross-border trucking, and how Canadian shippers and carriers should prepare.

item.title: Fire Season Hits the Highways: How BC's 2026 Wildfires Are Squeezing Freight Corridors
item.description: A wildfire near Lytton has already shut roughly 116 km of Highway 1, and BC Wildfire Service says 2026 is starting on worse drought than 2021. Here is what fire season does to BC freight corridors, what a closure costs a truck, and how carriers and shippers should plan around it.

item.title: Peace at Last? What the US-Iran Deal and a Reopened Strait of Hormuz Mean for Trucking
item.description: The US and Iran have reached a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the conflict, and oil is already down 20% from its 2026 peak. Here is what the peace deal could mean for diesel, freight capacity, and trucking rates, and how shippers should play the turn.

item.title: Iran and Israel Flare Up Again: How June 2026 Oil Whiplash Is Squeezing Small Carriers
item.description: Iran fired missiles at Israel again on June 8, sending Brent and Canadian diesel on another wild swing. Here is how the oil whiplash hits small carriers, how prices compare to last year, and what Keylink does to keep customer freight priced fairly.

item.title: Memorial Day 2026 Cargo Theft Surge: Why the Long Weekend Is the Riskiest Freight Window of Spring
item.description: Cargo theft is hitting records in 2026 and Memorial Day weekend is historically the worst long weekend of the spring. Here is what is driving the surge, the Canadian cross-border exposure, and how Keylink locks down high-risk loads.

item.title: Ontario's Truck Driver Training Audit: Why the Auditor General's Findings Should Change How Carriers Hire
item.description: Ontario's auditor general found private colleges falsifying records and licensing drivers who never learned left turns or emergency stops. Here is what carriers, shippers, and the industry should be doing in response.

item.title: Missiles Over the UAE: How Today's Dubai-Area Oil Strike Is Driving Canadian Diesel Past $2.20
item.description: A May 4 missile strike on a UAE petroleum facility near Dubai has pushed Brent past $116 and Canadian diesel north of $2.20 a litre. Here is what today's attack means for Canadian carriers and how Keylink is protecting its customers from the worst of it.

item.title: Carney, Trump and Calgary Trucking: How Keylink Is Helping Carriers Curve Canada's 2026 Trade Storm
item.description: Mark Carney has a majority government, a new Canada-US advisory council, and a CUSMA review starting July 1. Calgary trucking is paying the price of the tariffs in the meantime. Here is how Keylink is keeping the BC-Alberta lane moving.

item.title: Iran-US Peace Talks in Pakistan: Why the Hormuz Blockade Must End for Canadian Trucking
item.description: Pakistan is brokering a second round of Iran-US talks as the Hormuz blockade pushes Canadian diesel up 75%. Here is why these negotiations matter more to freight than any policy Ottawa has announced.

item.title: The Strait of Hormuz Crisis: What Trump's Iran Standoff Means for Global Shipping and Canadian Freight
item.description: 21 million barrels of oil transit the Strait of Hormuz every single day. Trump's maximum pressure campaign against Iran has placed this shipping lane at genuine risk. Here is what it means for Canadian fuel prices and freight costs.

item.title: The Canada-US Tariff War: What It Actually Costs Canadian Trucking in 2026
item.description: Border wait times up. Cross-border volumes down. Rates climbing. One year into Trump's 25% tariffs on Canadian goods, here is the full cost breakdown for carriers and shippers.

item.title: Canada's Trucking Workforce Crisis: Why the Driver Shortage Is Accelerating and What It Means for Freight Rates
item.description: Canada needs 40,000 more truck drivers by 2030. The demographics are locked in, the retirement wave has started, and the recruitment pipeline is failing. Here is the full picture and what shippers need to do.

item.title: Navigating Supply Chain Disruptions: Strategies for Canadian Shippers
item.description: Global disruptions have exposed real vulnerabilities in freight networks. These are the proven strategies Canadian shippers use to stay ahead when lanes get unpredictable.

item.title: 2025 in Review: The Year Canadian Trucking Was Reshaped by Tariffs
item.description: Eleven months into the most consequential year in cross-border freight in two decades. The tariffs, the diesel spikes, the carrier exits, and the carriers who came through stronger.

item.title: Cross-Border Freight in 2026: What Every Shipper Needs to Know
item.description: New regulations, updated CUSMA enforcement, and tighter border protocols are reshaping cross-border freight. Know exactly what changed before your next shipment crosses.

item.title: Peak Season 2025: How Tariffs and Capacity Shifts Are Reshaping Canadian Holiday Freight
item.description: The first full peak under the Trump tariff regime. Capacity is tighter, retail flows are rerouted, rates are climbing. Here is what Canadian shippers need to know before December.

item.title: 5 Ways to Optimize Your Freight Routes for Maximum Efficiency
item.description: Small routing decisions compound into major cost savings over time. These five tactics reduce empty miles, cut dwell time, and improve on-time delivery rates.

item.title: US Government Shutdown and Cross-Border Freight: What's Slowing at the Border
item.description: The US federal government shut down at midnight October 1. Two weeks in, CBP staffing reductions, USDA inspection delays and SBA financing freezes are rippling into Canadian cross-border freight.

item.title: Q3 2025 Canadian Freight Market: Carriers Surviving the Tariff Year
item.description: Three quarters into the tariff regime, Canadian freight has settled into a new normal. Spot rates have firmed, capacity has tightened, and carriers who restructured early are outperforming the field.

item.title: Winter Driving Protocols Every Freight Carrier Should Follow
item.description: Canadian winters demand more than good tires. This is how professional carriers build safety into every pre-trip inspection, dispatch decision, and delivery window.

item.title: BC Wildfires 2025: How a Second-Worst Fire Season Is Disrupting Western Canadian Freight Corridors
item.description: BC's 2025 wildfire season has scorched over 700,000 hectares, closed Highway 97, and strained BC-Alberta freight corridors. Here is how carriers and shippers are adjusting.
